atencao.d: Mechanism in which each token compares its query with the keys of the other tokens, turns the scores into weights with a softmax and receives the weighted average of the values. In a standard Transformer, it is the only sublayer where information crosses positions (in hybrids, linear attention and short convolutions also mix positions).

query-key-value.t: Query, key and value (Q, K, V)
query-key-value.d: The three linear projections of each token's vector: the query (\( q = xW_Q \)) is what the token is looking for, the key (\( k = xW_K \)) is how it advertises itself and the value (\( v = xW_V \)) is the content it delivers to whoever queries it.

produto-escalar-escalado.d: The standard form of attention: \( \operatorname{softmax}(QK^\top/\sqrt{d_h} + M)\,V \). Dividing by \( \sqrt{d_h} \) keeps the standard deviation of the scores close to 1 whatever the size of the head.

softmax.d: Function that turns real-valued scores into positive weights that sum to 1: \( a_j = e^{s_j}/\sum_k e^{s_k} \). It doesn't change if we add the same constant to every score, which is what lets us compute it without overflow by subtracting the maximum. It shows up in attention and in sampling.

softmax-estavel.d: Computing \( e^{s_j - m} \) with \( m = \max_k s_k \) instead of \( e^{s_j} \). The largest exponent becomes \( e^0 = 1 \), nothing overflows (FP16 already overflows at \( e^{11.1} \)) and the result is identical.

log-sum-exp.d: \( \operatorname{LSE}(s) = \ln\sum_j e^{s_j} = m + \ln\sum_j e^{s_j - m} \). Summarizes the “size” of a row of scores in a single number; with it, \( \ln a_j = s_j - \operatorname{LSE} \), and softmax pieces computed separately (tiles, split-K) can be merged exactly.

saturacao-softmax.d: When the scores are too spread out (standard deviation ≫ 1), the softmax becomes nearly one-hot: one key takes ~100% of the weight, the others get ~0 and their gradients vanish. This is what the \( 1/\sqrt{d_h} \) scale and QK-Norm prevent.

mascara-causal.d: Matrix added to the scores before the softmax, with 0 where \( j \le i \) and \( -\infty \) where \( j > i \): token \( i \) only sees tokens \( 0\ldots i \). It lets all positions train in parallel without “cheating” and guarantees that a token's K and V never change once computed (KV cache, prefix caching).

atencao-bidirecional.d: Attention without a causal mask: each position sees all the others in the span, including the later ones. It is the standard for vision towers and block drafters (DFlash2 with is_causal: false, DSpark). Serving with a mask different from the training one raises no error, it just degrades the result.

matriz-de-atencao.d: The matrix \( A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n} \) of weights after the softmax: row \( i \) says how much token \( i \) looks at each token \( j \) and sums to 1. There is one per head and per layer; modern kernels don't materialize it.

memoria-associativa.d: Content-addressed memory: it stores key→value pairs and, given a query similar to a key, returns the associated value. Attention is a “soft” version: it returns the average of the values weighted by the similarity of the query to each key; the query's norm plays the role of a temperature.

atencao-multicabeca.d: \( H \) attentions in parallel, each with its own \( d_h \)-dimensional projections; the outputs are concatenated and mixed by o_proj. Each head can look for a different relation at the same time. \( H \) is the config's num_attention_heads.

head-dim.d: Number of dimensions of each attention head. It sets the \( 1/\sqrt{d_h} \) scale, the KV bytes per token and the shape of the kernel tiles: 256 in Qwen3.8's QSA and in GLM-5.3's MLA (qk_head_dim), 512 in DeepSeek-V4, 128 in DFlash2. In modern models \( H\cdot d_h \) doesn't have to equal the hidden size.

o-proj.d: Attention's output projection: it takes the concatenation of the heads (\( H\cdot d_v \)) and returns a vector the size of the hidden, which is added to the residual stream. In GLM-5.3 it is [4096 × 16,384]; in DeepSeek-V4 it is split into groups (wo_a/wo_b). It is attention's “writer”, which is why abliteration modifies it.

complexidade-quadratica.d: With \( n \) tokens, each layer compares \( \sim n^2/2 \) query-key pairs per head: FLOPs \( \propto H(d_h+d_v)\,n^2 \) in prefill and, if materialized, a matrix of \( n^2 \) scores. In decode each new token reads the \( n \) previous keys. This is what motivates linear attention, sparse attention and latent KV.

attention-sink.d: (1) The phenomenon: models with pure softmax dump their “leftover” attention on the first token, whose value becomes ~0. (2) The explicit solution: a learned per-head logit \( \sigma_h \) that enters only the denominator, \( a_j = e^{s_j}/(e^{\sigma_h}+\sum_k e^{s_k}) \), letting the head “look at nothing”. Its neutral value is \( -\infty \) (DeepSeek-V4: attn_sink, 64 per layer).

atencao-com-gate.t: Attention with an output gate (gated attention)
atencao-com-gate.d: Each head's output is multiplied, element-wise, by \( \sigma(g) \), where \( g \) comes from an extra projection of the same token. The head can shut itself off, without a sink, and gains a nonlinearity between V and o_proj. In Qwen3.8 the gate comes from the extra half of q_proj [12,288 × 2560].

qk-norm.d: RMSNorm applied to each head of \( q \) and of \( k \) before the dot product (and before RoPE). It bounds the size of the scores by the learned gain and contains logit blow-ups during training, an alternative to tricks like qk-clip. Qwen3.8: q_norm/k_norm [256]; DeepSeek-V4: q normalized per head and kv_norm (the DeepSeek report credits this normalization for making qk-clip unnecessary).

exp2-log2e.d: GPUs have a native instruction for \( 2^x \). Since \( e^x = 2^{x\log_2 e} \), attention kernels multiply the scale by \( \log_2 e \approx 1.4427 \) once and use exp2 everywhere; the maximum and the LSE then live in base-2 units. The math doesn't change.
